journal.title: More Throughput Failed The Experience Gate
journal.summary: The corrected attribution test reached a decision: higher aggregate throughput did not excuse worse stalls.
journal.observation: The completed review observed at 17:09:09 UTC covers two users at 16K context per slot: 36 requests per variant across 12 required groups with three observations each. Aggregate workload rates were 16.179 tokens/s for the original reference, 22.385 for balanced Q6, and 22.354 for natural-lazy Engram. Both optimized controls failed the strict no-worse stall gate despite passing their accounting, quality, and final-slot self-checks. A representative balanced maximum content-chunk gap was 1.564s versus 0.751s; natural-lazy reached 1.533s versus 0.763s in another group.
journal.limitation: Content chunks are not guaranteed individual tokens. Three observations per group are small-sample tail estimates. Aggregate throughput is descriptive, not a per-user guarantee. No optimized winner was deployed from these results; the original reference remains the fallback.
journal.next: Use the rejected cases to isolate scheduling/interference costs. Qualify any later candidate against the same complete user/slot/role groups without weakening the acceptance gates.

journal.title: Lower Precision, A Controlled Comparison

journal.title: Long Context Works. Service Fit Still Matters.
journal.summary: A one-user recall milestone does not automatically translate into a two-user service.
journal.observation: A one-user recall screen at a 262,144-token context setting passed with 260,516 actual input tokens. The later local export also records a separate 260,498-input / 1,024-output request at 12.324 decode tokens/s. The two-user configuration at that context hit the GPU-memory-headroom safety limit.

journal.next: Repeat realistic long-document workloads, measure per-user latency and interference, and qualify the context that the intended service can actually sustain.

journal.title: Mapped To SSD Isn’t The Same As Reading SSD
journal.summary: Linux page caching makes Engram placement a measurement question, not a launch-flag assumption.
journal.observation: Natural lazy loading, manually warmed lazy loading, and eager CPU placement produced similar short-request screens. Manual warming reached only 18.15% whole-file page-cache residency.
journal.limitation: We have not established a fully DRAM-resident-versus-cold-SSD comparison. A memory mapping alone does not prove where each lookup is served.
journal.next: Correlate file residency, faults, process memory, and disk reads with request phases while holding the same Q8 table fixed.

journal.title: Prefill And Decode Need Different Explanations
journal.summary: Disabling selected gather paths affected prompt processing much more than generation.
journal.observation: At 1,955 input and 512 output tokens, three-request medians fell from 714.844 to 478.586 prefill tokens/s with XMX gather/dequant-GEMM paths disabled. Decode remained near 35.7 tokens/s.
journal.limitation: This control does not disable every XMX operation or measure XMX occupancy. It is not proof of bandwidth saturation or a driver defect.
journal.next: Use the newly captured execution/dispatch and routing records to test the mechanism. Full-model GPU kernel durations still need a validated capture; keep instrumented results out of performance ranking.
